End Event

General Concept: An End Event in BPMN marks the end of a process or subprocess. It indicates where the process flow stops and can optionally trigger actions (message, error, etc.).

 

TaktX Implementation: In TaktX, an End Event finalizes the process instance, cleans up variable scope, and can trigger outbound actions (message, error, escalation). Output mappings using FEEL expressions can be used to prepare final data. The engine supports error and escalation end events for advanced process control.

Usage & Options in TaktX:
An End Event in TaktX allows you to:

  • Mark the completion of a process or subprocess, signaling normal or special completion (error, escalation, message, etc.).
  • Define output mappings using FEEL expressions to set final variables or results.
  • Trigger outbound actions such as messages, errors, or escalations.
  • Clean up variable scope and finalize process data.
  • Monitor process completion and audit results via the TaktX client.
  • Configure end event type to match business requirements.

 

Example: Payment Failure Handling with Error End Event

 

This example shows a process where an Error End Event is used to handle a failed payment. If payment fails, the process throws an error, which can be caught by a boundary event for compensation or alternative flow. This demonstrates robust error handling in TaktX.

Tips & Tricks:

  • Use output mappings to set final variables or results.
  • Configure end event type to match business requirements.
  • Document expected outcomes and actions.

Pitfalls:

  • Unconfigured end events may not trigger required actions.
  • Missing output mappings can cause data loss.
